result: Endogenous GABAAR subunits in mouse cerebellar membranes segregate into two major complexes on BN-PAGE: a GARLHed complex (α1/β/γ2 with GARLH4/NL2) migrating at 720 kDa, and a GARLHless GABAAR (α6/β/δ) migrating at 480 kDa.
evaluation: Claims C21-C26 collectively demonstrate clear segregation of GABAAR subunits into two distinct complexes using BN-PAGE. The data in Figure 1 directly show differential migration patterns of subunits (δ/α6 at 480 kDa; γ2/α1/GARLH4/NL2 at 720 kDa), with β2/3 distributed equally between both complexes. This is consistent with prior work (C24) and provides strong biochemical evidence for the two-complex model.

result: Functional GABAAR pentamers can be reconstituted in Xenopus oocytes, migrating at 520 kDa on BN-PAGE, as confirmed by comparison with concatenated pentamers and electrophysiological recordings.
evaluation: Claims C27-C33 establish the oocyte system as a valid model for studying GABAAR assembly. The co-migration of oligomers and concatenated pentamers at 520 kDa (C32), combined with functional GABA-evoked currents (C29), provides strong evidence that the 520 kDa complex represents pentameric GABAARs. The absence of homomers (C31) further validates the specificity of heteromeric assembly.

result: α1 and α6 subunits possess intrinsic signals that cause them to segregate into distinct GABAAR pentamers, independent of non-α/β subunits (γ2 and δ).
evaluation: Claims C35-C37 and C75 demonstrate α1/α6 segregation through antibody shift assays in both oocytes (C35) and γ2/δ double knockout cerebella (C37). The finding that segregation persists even when both α subunits can assemble with GARLH/NL2 (C75) strongly supports the conclusion that segregation is encoded by intrinsic properties of the α subunits themselves, not by differential association with non-α/β subunits.

result: γ2 is essential for native GABAAR assembly with GARLHs, as demonstrated by antibody shift assays in cerebellum and elimination of GARLHed complexes in γ2-deficient cultured neurons.
evaluation: Claims C38-C42 provide converging evidence from multiple experimental systems. Antibody shift assays show nearly complete incorporation of γ2 into GARLHed complexes in cerebellum (C39), and genetic elimination of γ2 in cultured neurons completely abolishes GARLHed complexes (C41). Combined with prior work (C42), this strongly supports the essential role of γ2 in GARLH assembly.

result: In γ2 GC-KO mice, GABAARs are redistributed from synaptic to extrasynaptic sites, and GABAAR-mediated synaptic transmission is almost completely eliminated.
evaluation: Claims C47-C53 demonstrate the functional consequences of γ2 deletion through multiple complementary approaches. Immunohistochemistry shows reduced α1 colocalization with the synaptic marker VGAT and increased colocalization with the glomerular marker GluN1 (C49-C50). Electrophysiology confirms near-complete elimination of sIPSCs (C51-C52). These data strongly support the conclusion that γ2 is required for synaptic GABAAR localization and function in adult brain.

result: γ2 directs the synaptic localization of the inhibitory scaffold gephyrin in the adult brain.
evaluation: Claims C54-C56 show that in γ2 GC-KO mice, gephyrin colocalization with both VGAT (inhibitory presynaptic marker) and GluN1 (glomerular marker) is substantially reduced. This demonstrates that γ2 is required not only for GABAAR synaptic localization but also for proper gephyrin clustering at inhibitory synapses, extending prior findings from cultured neurons to the adult brain.

result: δ suppresses synaptic localization of α6-containing GABAARs in the brain, as demonstrated by redistribution of α6 from extrasynaptic to synaptic sites in δ GC-KO mice.
evaluation: Claims C58-C64 provide strong immunohistochemical evidence for δ's role in controlling α6 localization. In δ GC-KO mice, α6 forms clusters at the glomerular periphery that overlap with VGAT (C60, C62), contrasting with the diffuse extrasynaptic distribution in controls (C61). The specificity of α6 signal is confirmed using α6 KO controls (C59). This demonstrates that δ normally prevents α6 synaptic localization.

result: δ inhibits the incorporation of α6 into γ2-containing GARLHed complexes in vivo, as shown by α6 incorporation into GARLHed complexes in δ GC-KO but not in control or γ2/δ double knockout cerebella.
evaluation: Claims C65-C72 demonstrate through BN-PAGE that α6 incorporates into GARLHed complexes only in δ GC-KO mice (C65), not in controls or double knockouts (C66-C67). The upregulation of GARLHed complex components (γ2, GARLH4, NL2) without concomitant α1 upregulation (C69) and the appearance of α1/γ2 in GARLHless complexes (C70) suggest that GARLH/NL2 becomes limiting in δ GC-KO. This provides strong evidence that δ normally sequesters α6 away from γ2-containing complexes.

result: δ is sufficient to inhibit α6 incorporation into γ2-containing GABAARs in heterologous cells, as demonstrated by antibody shift assays in oocytes.
evaluation: Claims C73-C74 show that in oocytes, α6 preferentially assembles with δ over γ2 when both are present, and both α1 and α6 can associate with GARLH4/NL2 when coexpressed with γ2 but not δ. This demonstrates that δ is sufficient to prevent α6/γ2 assembly in a heterologous system, complementing the in vivo findings.

result: There exists an assembly pathway for α6-containing GARLHed complexes that is normally silenced by δ, and activation of this pathway in δ's absence increases inhibitory synaptic transmission by allowing α6 pentamers to localize to synapses.
evaluation: Claims C76-C78 synthesize the findings into a coherent model. The data showing α6 incorporation into GARLHed complexes and synaptic localization in δ GC-KO mice, combined with prior work showing increased α6-mediated IPSCs in δ KO mice (C77, citing Accardi et al. 2015), strongly support the existence of a normally suppressed assembly pathway. This represents a major conceptual advance in understanding GABAAR assembly regulation.

result: Background knowledge on GABAAR structure, diversity, and localization establishes the context for the study.
evaluation: Claims C1-C15 represent established knowledge about GABAARs, properly cited to prior literature. These claims provide necessary background but are not novel findings of this study. They establish that GABAARs are pentamers with diverse subunit compositions, that specific subtypes localize to synaptic vs. extrasynaptic sites, and that the rules governing assembly are incompletely understood.

result: GARLHs are auxiliary subunits that form complexes with GABAARs and NL2, and are essential for synaptic localization and function.
evaluation: Claims C16-C20 summarize prior work on GARLHs, primarily from the authors' previous publication (Yamasaki et al., 2017). These claims establish the functional importance of GARLHs for GABAAR synaptic localization and provide the foundation for investigating GABAAR-GARLH assembly rules. While not novel to this study, they are essential context.

result: Speculative explanations and hypotheses about molecular mechanisms and physiological implications.
evaluation: Claims C28, C82, and C84 represent speculative interpretations. C28 proposes possible explanations for size differences between oocyte and brain complexes. C82 suggests why conventional and conditional δ KO mice show different phenotypes. C84 hypothesizes that δ expression changes could regulate synaptic strength. While these are reasonable hypotheses, they lack direct experimental support in this study and should be tested in future work.

result: Methodological considerations and structural knowledge about GABAARs inform the experimental approach.
evaluation: Claims C85-C90 provide important methodological context (BN-PAGE limitations) and structural knowledge (subunit arrangements, existing structural studies). These are properly cited to prior work and help interpret the experimental results. While not novel findings, they are important for understanding the study's approach and limitations.

result: Generation of viable conditional knockout mice circumvents the lethality of conventional γ2 knockout.
evaluation: Claims C96-C98 describe the generation of conditional knockout mice. The viability of γ2/δ GC-DKO and γ2 GC-KO mice with normal body weight (C97-C98) is directly demonstrated. This represents an important technical advance enabling the in vivo studies, though it is a methodological rather than mechanistic finding.

result: Validation of α6 KO mice confirms expected changes in GABAAR subunit expression.
evaluation: Claims C99-C100 validate the α6 KO model by confirming elimination of α6 and expected reductions in δ and β2/3, consistent with prior literature. This is important quality control for the study but represents confirmation of known findings rather than novel discoveries.

result: Comparison of conventional and conditional δ KO mice reveals differences in compensatory changes.
evaluation: Claims C79-C81 compare protein expression changes between conventional and conditional δ KO mice. While γ2 upregulation is observed in both (C79), α1 and β3 changes differ (C80-C81), possibly due to timing of Cre expression (C82). This provides important context for interpreting the δ GC-KO phenotype but is primarily descriptive.

result: Partial reduction of γ2 and GARLHed complexes in γ2 GC-KO cerebella is explained by expression in non-granule cells.
evaluation: Claim C101 explains why γ2 and GARLHed complexes are only partially reduced in γ2 GC-KO cerebella, attributing this to expression in Purkinje cells and other non-granule neurons. This is a reasonable interpretation supported by prior literature (Laurie et al., 1992) and is important for correctly interpreting the knockout phenotype.
